title: rwb-integration outbound-file capability: ACE read path, INT-25 source table, data-lake retirement, JOB-10 and JOB-11 split, operation naming, alert event names, deliverFile manifest and job catalog rows not settled
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8, 9, 11, 13, 16, 29, 31, 32, 33, 37, 41, 43, 44 and 45; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T3.1, T4, T5.2, T6.2 and T-A.1; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5, A1.6 and A2.7; Ownership Map tables (interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog, debt_sale_account, notice, document) and API (four P2 admin rows); legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 12, 13 and 15; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.5, §R5.7 and §R9
section: §1 Story, §2 Business rationale, §7 Acceptance criteria, §8 Business rules, §11 Data, §12.2 REST consumed, §12.6 Schedules, §12.7 Tables owned, §15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the unsettled and conflicting points of this story. (1) ACE read path: Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37 and 45 and ADR-010 say only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views, while TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T5.2 and T6.2 say P2 reads them directly; by R-PREC the architecture wins and the TSD wording is superseded, so every ACE fact is one REST call to the rwb-source-data contract with a 2 s timeout. (2) INT-25 source: the legacy AC1 builds the synthetic tape from debt_sale_account, which the Ownership Map gives to S6 rwb-debtsale, so the tape rows arrive in the deliverFile manifest and are never read here. (3) Data lake: the legacy story and the FSD A1.5 still describe the INT-19 reporting extract and the INT-20 decision feed as lake files with JOB-13 and JOB-15, while DP-17 and Architecture v5 slides 2, 8, 37 and 44 remove the lake; the extract is delivered to rwb-reporting through deliverFile and the decision feed is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision, and the lake statements are retired rather than restated. (4) Job ownership: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-10 to rwb-comms + integration while Architecture v5 slide 16 gives the deliverFile activity and the file windows to rwb-integration alone, and the legacy story assumes one Quartz scheduler for JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13 and JOB-15; the split taken is JOB-11 as the platform outbox relay, JOB-10 as a bank-Airflow window with the file built and sent by rwb-integration, and JOB-13 and JOB-15 removed. (5) Operation naming: Architecture v5 slide 16 names GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, while the TSD P2 v3 appendix and the Ownership Map name GET /admin/outbound-items, POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend, GET /admin/outbox/deliveries and POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend; the TSD and Ownership Map names are used and the slide 16 naming is superseded. (6) Alert names: the legacy story alerts on the events rwb.integration.outbound.held and rwb.integration.outbound.failed, which are not event names under DP-14, so the held-file alert is a rule over the held-item series and the failed-file alert a rule over FileFailed and the EXCEPTION status. (7) Manifest: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 16 fix an activity deliverFile(manifest) and a claim-check manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, but not the full payload, the return element or the internal split with a workflow. (8) Job catalog: no source says whether job_catalog holds rows for JOB-10 and JOB-11 after the slide 44 split, so this key writes none and leaves it to the job catalog read. (9) Message wording: the FSD P2 Integration v3 rewrites MSG-P1-001 and outranks the story master, so the FSD wording is used.
evidence: TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 'P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly and calls nothing in P1 for inbound data' and T6.2 'The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views only' against Architecture v5 slide 9 'only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views' and slide 37 'Views read only by rwb-source-data'; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 rows INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI' and INT-20 'COLLINS, through the data lake' against Architecture v5 slide 2 'Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19/INT-20 are removed'; Architecture v5 slide 44 row JOB-10 'rwb-comms + integration | Airflow file window + workers' against slide 16 'TMP Act: deliverFile(manifest), receiveFile · Airflow window: WIN file 16:00, buyer files per lot'; Architecture v5 slide 16 'REST GET /interface-runs (operations) · POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry' against TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 API-P2-001 to API-P2-004 and the Ownership Map rows; Ownership Map debt_sale_account 'S6 owns lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer' against legacy RWB-E1-007 AC1 'builds the synthetic tape of 120 accounts from debt_sale_account and v_ace_account'; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 15 'the Log Analytics alert rule on events rwb.integration.outbound.held and rwb.integration.outbound.failed' against Architecture v5 slide 16 'EVT rwb.integration.events.v1: FileDelivered, FileFailed'.
area: Integration (P2) outbound files: ACE read path, source-table ownership, job split, API naming and alerts
proposed: Build the outbound-file capability in rwb-integration on the service base /api/recovery/integration/v1, with interface_config and outbound_item as its own tables and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects as library objects in rwb_integration (DP-01, DP-02, DP-09, DP-15). Read every ACE fact through the rwb-source-data contract one hop and 2 s, and record that the TSD P2 v3 direct-view wording is superseded by Architecture v5 and ADR-010. Take the INT-25 tape rows from the deliverFile manifest that rwb-debtsale sends. Retire the lake statements of INT-19, INT-20, JOB-13 and JOB-15: the extract is delivered to rwb-reporting through deliverFile and the decision feed is Kafka ingest in rwb-decision. Keep JOB-11 as the platform relay and JOB-10 as a bank-Airflow window with the file built and sent here, and register no Schedule for either window. Use the four TSD and Ownership Map admin paths and record slide 16's /interface-runs naming as superseded. Restate the two alerts as rules over the held-item series and over FileFailed, owned by the operations story. Fix the manifest and the return element in the contract story and re-confirm them with rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale and rwb-reporting. Load the four interface rows as reference data; leave the job_catalog rows to the job catalog read. Confirm with the ACE team that rwb_integration needs no grant on the recovery schema.

title: Outbound-file contract: deliverFile manifest and return, notice-fact read of rwb-comms, JSON field names and problem body, event schema subject and compatibility level not fixed by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 17 and 41; TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Ownership Map tables (notice, interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog) and API (four P2 admin rows); legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 11, 12 and 13; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG sections 12.2 and 12.5; Template and Rules v1 §R9
section: §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §12.2 REST consumed, §12.3 Events published, §12.5 Workflows and activities, §13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the shape-level points that no source fixes for this contract. (1) The manifest of deliverFile: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 16 fix a claim-check manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count and an activity named deliverFile(manifest), but not the interface ID, the business date, the case IDs, the idempotency key, the claim-check link or the requesting service. (2) The return element of deliverFile and the internal split between the activity and a local workflow. (3) The notice-fact read behind INT-14: the legacy story read the notice table in process, notice belongs to P6, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 no notice-fact read, so the operation exists in this contract with no path, query or field name in any source. (4) The JSON field names of the four admin responses and the detail texts of the problem body. (5) The schema-registry subject of rwb.integration.events.v1 and its compatibility level. (6) Whether job_catalog holds rows for JOB-10 and JOB-11. (7) The naming difference between Architecture v5 slide 16 (/interface-runs) and the TSD appendix and Ownership Map (/admin/outbound-items and /admin/outbox/deliveries), recorded as a conflict in CG-B-P2-01-E1007-1 and applied here.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Manifest: fileId, batchId, sha256, record count' and slide 16 'TMP Act: deliverFile(manifest), receiveFile'; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 'REST POST /notices (request) · GET /cases/{id}/notices' and no notice read by ID; TSD P2 v3 T-A.2 gives the four operations with their query parameters and error codes but no body shape; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 gives the columns of interface_config, outbound_item, processed_event, idempotency_key, outbox_event, outbox_delivery and job_catalog; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 11 reads notice.sent_date (DF-LEG-019) and notice.person_key (DF-LEG-030) from the notice table in process; the sibling integration story states that the manifest and the claim-check handoff are 'Not specified in the source documents'.
area: Integration (P2) outbound files: contract shapes, consumed notice read and event registry
proposed: Fix the manifest, the return element and the three typed failures in RWB-P2-E1007-CON and re-confirm them with rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale and rwb-reporting. Fix the notice-fact read in the rwb-comms contract with the notice ID, the sent date, the person key and the document ID. Publish one RFC 9457 problem-details body for the four admin operations with the six status codes of the TSD appendix. Fix the JSON names of the four responses in the OpenAPI document. Fix the registry subject and the compatibility level with the platform event owner. Leave the job_catalog rows to the job catalog read. Take the TSD and Ownership Map admin paths and record slide 16's naming as superseded.

title: Outbound egress infrastructure: endpoint names, accounts, folders, receiver ranges, PGP key identifiers, staging names, file-size limit, transfer timeout and rotation period not specified in any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 16, 32 and 35; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052 and NFR-053; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.1; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3; RWB-PLT-N012-INF
section: §3 Preconditions, §6 INVEST check, §8 Business rules, §10 Authority, §11 Data, §13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the infrastructure values of this key. Architecture v5 slides 8, 11, 16 and 32 name the two outbound interfaces (INT-14 WIN registered mail and INT-25 debt buyers), the MFT/SFTP transport with PGP for a party outside the bank and a claim-check link for one file for 15 minutes, and slides 11 and 35 require private access, workload identity and keys in the key store; no source names the endpoint hosts, ports, accounts, folders, file patterns per environment, the receiver ranges, the PGP key identifiers or fingerprints, the staging location names, the maximum file size, the transfer timeout, the connection and read timeouts, the concurrent transfer limit or the rotation period. The 15 minutes of Architecture v5 slide 11 is the validity of the claim-check link and not a transfer budget, so it cannot be used as the timeout.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Transport: Blob + MFT/SFTP; PGP for outside parties' and 'Identity: SAS link, one file, 15 minutes' with no size or timeout value; Architecture v5 slide 35 lists zero trust and private access without naming a range; NFR-052 'Secrets are held in the key store and never in code, configuration files or prompts' without a rotation period; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3 'The SFTP outbound folders exist in DEV and SIT, with credentials in the key store (NFR-052)' and no folder name.
area: Integration (P2) outbound egress: MFT/SFTP endpoints, keys, network and budgets
proposed: Provision the two endpoints per environment with one receiver and one key each, hold the credentials, private keys and certificates in the key store behind the rwb-integration workload identity, apply the private DNS records and the egress allow-list, stage the file with its manifest and its sha256, and set the size, timeout and concurrency budgets as environment values. Fix every value with the bank MFT team, the network team and security, and record the rotation period in the key-rotation runbook.

title: Outbound-file deployment: chart values, replica counts, KEDA threshold, lag and alert thresholds, dashboard names, build ID format, Airflow trigger contract of the two file windows and the message identifiers of the lag and window alerts not specified in any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 9, 16, 31, 32, 33, 41, 44 and 45; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11; ADR-023; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 and T-A.1; RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG section 12.6; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s14 and §R9
section: §11 Data, §12.6 Schedules, §14 Validation and messages, §13 Solution plan (alert mapping and artefacts)
description: One combined row for the deployment values and identifiers of this key. Architecture v5 slides 9, 33 and 41 fix the topic settings, the KEDA scaling shape and one login per service, and slides 16, 31, 32 and 44 fix the 16:00 WIN window and the per-lot buyer window as bank-Airflow work with rwb-integration building and sending the files, but no source fixes the chart values, the replica counts, the resource sizes, the KEDA backlog threshold, the consumer quotas, the lag and alert thresholds, the dashboard names, the build ID format or the trigger contract of the two windows (the call, its parameters and its idempotency key). The lag alert and the window and endpoint alert also have no message identifier and no agreed text in the source set, so both carry the §R9 placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names them.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-10 WIN notices 16:00 rwb-comms + integration Airflow file window + workers' and slide 32 'rwb-integration still builds the files and manifests; Airflow owns the window, the transfer and the retry' with no call contract; Architecture v5 slide 9 'Kafka: topic per service rwb.<name>.events.v1, 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode, outbox and inbox, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt' with no lag threshold; Temporal and Drools design slide 11 names worker versioning and a build ID without a format; the legacy RWB-E1-007 section 14 lists MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-GEN-005, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P2-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 and no lag or window alert identifier.
area: Integration (P2) outbound files: deployment values, Airflow windows and alert identifiers
proposed: Set the chart values, the replica counts, the KEDA backlog threshold, the lag and alert thresholds and the build ID format as environment values of the operations story. Confirm the two windows with the bank Airflow owner as calls to the requesting services on their own APIs, and record that the deployment registers no Schedule and no timer for either. Fix the trigger contract of the two windows and the message identifiers of the lag and window alerts with the Airflow owner and the platform observability owner, and keep the §R9 placeholder until they are named.

title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over: the mount of the step, the split across four owners, the consumed contract paths, the run summary store and the level of the decision record are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001; Ownership Map v1 (interaction, efs_ledger_outcome and reconciliation_result to P1; recovery_case and case_account to P3; decision_log_entry to P7; GET /admin/jobs, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, GET /data-products/freshness and POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions to P1); FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 (inbound source loads and EFS out of scope) and AC-EXC-P2-007-07; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 (P2 reads the views) and T5.2 (P2 calls nothing in P1 for inbound data); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15, 16, 41, 43, 44 and 45; RWB-ITG-E2001-ITG section 3 and section 11
description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The legacy story is one Quartz job inside one service; under D-RCV-60 the same journey is four owners, and the split is fixed only by the plan, the Ownership Map and RWB-ITG-E2001-ITG: case creation, the account link and CaseCreated to rwb-case; the EFS history read and the interaction append to rwb-source-data; the central ledger to rwb-decision; the hand-over step, the group builder and the run summary stay with rwb-integration. (2) Two sources place the work elsewhere: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 puts every inbound source load, EFS included, out of P2 scope because ACE ingests it, and TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2 still has P2 reading the ACE views directly and calling nothing in P1; both are superseded by DP-05 and ADR-010, and the conflict is recorded, not hidden. (3) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login. (4) The paths, query parameters and JSON field names of the consumed rwb-source-data operations for the eligible accounts, the customer row and the reconciliation result are not in any source, and neither is the rwb-case case-creation path (the Ownership Map publishes GET /cases and POST /cases/{caseId}/actions but no create operation), although the legacy interface CaseCreation.createOrLink names the operation. (5) JOB-02 stays rwb-case's per the Ownership Map and Arch v5 slide 44, while the legacy story started JOB-02 for the hand-over; the step therefore runs on AceDataReady in rwb-integration and the rerun operation POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun is P1's, so the refusal of a second start is split between P1's door and this step's run lock. (6) The legacy run summary was written to reconciliation_result and to the batch step; in the target reconciliation_result is P1's and job_catalog holds a catalogue row, not a run, so no table of rwb-integration holds a run summary. (7) The legacy story left the creation decision to the decision log writer; with DP-03 each owner writes its own record, and no source says whether the hand-over step writes a record of its own run or only the case owner writes one. (8) MSG-P1-001 is worded differently in the legacy story and in FSD P2 Integration v3 VR-P2-001-1.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 section 4 step 1 (JOB-02 starts when AceDataReady arrives) and step 9 (run summary to reconciliation_result); section 12 (Job JOB-02, HandoverRun, and the four in-process interfaces CaseCreation, InteractionLedger, AccountQuery, EfsHistoryQuery); section 13 (HandoverJob, no new table, processed_event and reconciliation_result written). TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 ('P2 reads source data only through recovery.v_ace_* views') and T5.2 ('P2 reads the views in T1.1 directly and calls nothing in P1 for inbound data'). FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 ('Out of scope: Every inbound source load: ALS, SCBPDM, EFS ...') and VR-P2-001-1 (MSG-P1-001 '{product} is from {date}. Today's data is not yet complete.'). Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, mechanism AceDataReady -> DailyCaseRun) and slide 45 ('Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010)'). Ownership Map v1 rows for interaction, efs_ledger_outcome, reconciliation_result, recovery_case, case_account, decision_log_entry, job_catalog and the four P1 operations.
area: Integration ownership, consumed contracts and run record
proposed: Keep the split recorded by RWB-ITG-E2001-ITG and the Ownership Map and mark TSD P2 v3 T5.2 and the P2 inbound exclusion as superseded by DP-05 and ADR-010 in the Service Contract Catalog; agree the consumed operation paths and field names at the contract review of RWB-P2-E2001-CON with the P1 and P3 owners; hold the run summary in the activity result, one local decision record and the REC-01 row written through P1, with no table of rwb-integration; name the login before the rwb_integration baseline is created.

title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over contract: the activity contract, the consumed element shapes, the provided surface and the fakes have no source text
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001 section 12; RWB-P2-E2001-APP; RWB-P2-E2001-CON; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P2 IN: GET /interface-runs, POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry; OUT: FileDelivered, FileFailed); TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1; Ownership Map v1
description: The contract this slice needs does not exist in the source set. (1) The legacy story fixes a Java interface HandoverRun with one method returning a summary of read, created, linked, repeats, held and gap dates, and four in-process interfaces; nothing fixes a workflow name, activity names, inputs, outputs, a retry policy or a summary element list, so every one of them is a default of this story. (2) Architecture v5 slide 16 and TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 give rwb-integration only the interface-run operations and the outbound-file events; no source gives a hand-over operation, and the step is event-started, so the slice provides no REST operation at all. (3) The element names of the six consumed rwb-source-data operations, the rwb-case case-creation answer (created or linked, linked from, is primary) and the decision-record failure class are not in any source. (4) The error mapping from a failing owner answer to MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-GEN-006 is implied by the legacy exception table and by the FSD exception flows, and is fixed here as a default. (5) MSG-P1-001 has two wordings; the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording is used and the legacy wording is not repaired.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 section 12 ('Published interface built (package recovery.integration.handover.api): public interface HandoverRun { HandoverSummary run(LocalDate businessDate); }') and the exception table MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002. FSD P2 Integration v3 AC-EXC-P2-007-03, AC-EXC-P2-007-06, AC-EXC-P2-007-07 and VR-P2-001-1. Architecture v5 slide 16 (P2 contract, no hand-over path) and slide 44 (JOB-02 with rwb-case). TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 API-P2-001 to API-P2-014 (no hand-over operation).
proposed: Fix the workflow, the nine activities, the twelve summary elements and the retry policy in contract/handover-run-activities.yaml; fix the six P1 elements and the P3 element in the two consumed contracts with the element names of this story as the default; carry the placeholder for every path and field name the source does not give; publish the six fakes from the owners' OpenAPI documents and fail the build on drift.

title: rwb-integration EFS hand-over deployment: the values, the alert identifiers, the dashboard series and the runbook have no source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5 and 14; RWB-P2-E2001-OPS; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32, 33 and 41; Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023; Non Functional Specification v3
description: The deployment of the step is a new artefact with no source text. (1) The legacy story names one feature flag and one hold time; nothing gives replica counts, resource sizes, probe paths and timings, lag thresholds, alert thresholds, consumer group name, retry intervals or the build ID format, so all of them are environment values and placeholders. (2) The legacy story raises a late-batch alert and an incident, and the FSD names MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-001, MSG-P2-006 and MSG-P7-003; no source names a message id for a lagging hand-over group or for a consumed AceDataReady that started no run, so both carry the placeholder. (3) No source names the dashboard series of the hand-over or its dimensions; ADR-023 fixes observability per service and the six series here — accounts read, cases created, accounts linked, repeats, held, gap dates — are the default. (4) No source names the runbook entries, their owner roles or the runbook location. (5) The smoke-run fixture owner and the synthetic business date are not given.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5 (X2, X6, X7) and 14 (MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P2-006, MSG-P4-002); section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.efs-handover). Architecture v5 slide 33 (rwb-comms and rwb-integration share the 16:00 window) and slide 41 (one login, one topic, one queue, one schema per service). Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-023 (observability per service). Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052, NFR-053 and NFR-054 (secrets, encryption, pipeline checks).
proposed: Fix the chart, the one consumer group, the registration step, the migration step, the six series, the four alerts and the four runbook entries in this story; keep every environment value in a values file and every missing message id as a placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it; review the runbook with the on-call rota before the release date.

title: rwb-integration ACE plan status: the login, the account resolution, the interface field types, the meaning of live and messageCode, the two settings, the connection-matrix rows and the ownership split are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-002; Ownership Map v1 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status owner P2; interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog owner P2; lov_value, reference_row, parameter_catalog, parameter_value owner P3; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, decision_log_entry owner P7); API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status and the PlanStatus schema; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16, 24, 29, 37, 41, 43, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 12, 14 and 27; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration v3.md (scope and REQ-DRI-013); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; RWB-P3-E2002-APP; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG
description: One combined gap covers what this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery service identity. (2) The account numbers of the case: the operation is case-scoped and takes the case reference only, while the ACE interface is keyed by account number, so the accounts have to be read first; no source states that the read calls the rwb-case case read, and the work package's contract row names only the parameters, reference-data and rule-catalog contracts. (3) The field types, lengths, required flags, null rules and query shapes of the case read, of the reference-data and parameter answers, of the authorise answer and of the remaining RestructurePlanQuery elements are given nowhere; only the four plan element names are. (4) The meaning of live and messageCode is split across sources: the API Specification carries both fields, the legacy story says live is true when read from ACE now, and neither says who fills the message when the live read fails; the case side needs the flag to choose between the two answers. (5) The two settings rwb.ace.plan.batch-size = 500 and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms = 2000 are legacy properties recorded as an assumption under DL11, while DP-06 makes parameters rwb-case data; no source states which owner carries them or how they are read. (6) The connection matrix gives P2 no row to ACE Common and no row to P3, and no row from P3 to P2, although the interface call, the account resolution and the daily call all exist; the omission is a defect of the matrix, not of the design. (7) The ownership split is fixed only by the plan and the Ownership Map: the ACE read and the live answer here, the stored status, the compare, the route state, the rules, the task, the timer, the decision record and the panel in rwb-case, the rights in rwb-access and the package in rwb-decision. (8) The routing of the daily call: the sibling story makes the plan-status step a step of JOB-02 owned by rwb-case, the integration harness lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration, and the job map gives JOB-02 to rwb-case; the sibling and the job map agree and the harness row is the outlier. (9) The stored fallback: the legacy story answers the stored status from the same endpoint, the target splits it into the rwb-case stored answer and this live answer, and the composite route that merges them has no published path or merge order.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 2 (the case list with account numbers through the P3 CaseQuery), step 3 (statusFor in batches of 500, assumed; DL11), step 8 (the endpoint reads ACE live with a 2-second timeout and falls back to the stored status) and section 12 (PlanStatus: planRef, status, statusDate, live, messageCode; RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor returning planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate); section 13 (properties rwb.ace.plan.batch-size and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms, assumed; DL11) and section 17 (no read of another module's tables, ACE data only through the interface). title: The plan-status contract baseline: the accountNo field, the meaning and owner of live and messageCode, the interface null rules, the consumed read shapes, the composite route and the two specification conflicts are not fixed by any one source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-002; Ownership Map v1 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status owner P2, basis API Specification v4 and TSD v5 P2 appendix T-A); API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status, the PlanStatus schema and x-capability Case record R; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 10, 11, 12, 13, 16, 41, 43, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11 and 27; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; RWB-P3-E2002-APP; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG
description: One combined gap covers the six things a contract cannot be faked without. (1) The answer shape: the API Specification PlanStatus carries planRef, status, statusDate, live and messageCode and no accountNo, while the legacy interface answer carries accountNo and the sibling case story joins on it; this contract adds the field and nothing in the source set settles whether it belongs in the resource. (2) The two flag fields: live and messageCode have a type and no rule; the legacy story says live is true when read from ACE now, the sibling story answers live false with MSG-P2-008 and the stored date, and no source says which provider fills the message, so the two-provider resource has no agreed rule. (3) The interface: the legacy story publishes the statusFor signature and four element names, and nothing about the null rules, the empty answer, the error classes, the batch boundary or the retry, all of which the app story has to implement. (4) The consumed reads: the case read, the authorise answer and the two reference answers have no paths, no element names and no types in any source; the reference-data and parameter contracts are named by DP-07 and DP-06 and their shapes are pending. (5) The composite route: the case record plan section is composed at the edge from this answer and the stored answer of rwb-case, and no source gives the route path, the merge order or the field precedence. (6) The two specification conflicts: the Technical Specification reads v_ace_plan with a fallback to the case columns, which ADR-010, DP-05 and the view rule refuse, and the Ownership Map and the API Specification keep the operation with P2 while the base changes to the integration base; both are reconciled here and recorded, not silently applied.

title: The plan-status deployment values, the ACE endpoint and certificate references, the two setting values at run time, the trigger wiring, the alert thresholds, the mapping of the no-package condition and the fixture owner are not fixed in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 16, 20, 24, 33, 41, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 12 and 27; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rulings on interface_config, job_catalog, parameter_catalog, reference_row and feature_flag); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1, T7 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; ADR-023; RWB-P2-E2002-CON; RWB-P2-E2002-APP
description: The deployment needs nine values or rules that no source fixes. (1) The rwb-integration identity name and its secret reference are not stated; only DP-02 states that one login per service exists. (2) The ACE common module endpoint, its certificate, its network path and its per-environment availability are not in any source, and the interface is not an interface_config row, so the release has no table to read them from. (3) The two settings have no stated run-time owner: the legacy story records them as service properties under DL11, DP-06 makes parameters rwb-case data, and the deployment has to know which of the two wins in an environment. (4) The budget rule is not stated: the operation must refuse inside the caller's 2 s budget, so a timeout value longer than the budget is a release defect, and no source gives the margin. (5) The trigger wiring is not written down: the calling paths are the rwb-case activity and the composite route, no P2 Schedule exists, and the integration harness nevertheless lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration. (6) The alert thresholds of the unavailable rate, the refusal rates, the unknown-status count and the duration against the budget are not stated, and the platform alert catalogue carries message identifiers, not values. (7) The no-package-in-force condition has no home here: this service never evaluates a package, so no series, alert or runbook entry of this release can observe it, and the mapping has to name its owners instead. (8) The dashboard dimensions, the retention of the series, the replica counts, the resource sizes and the probe timings have no baseline. (9) The owner of the synthetic fixtures of the smoke run is not stated.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 16 (P2 IN GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, OUT FileDelivered and FileFailed, with no ACE Common cell in the row) and slide 41 (schema rwb_integration, base /api/recovery/integration/v1, topic and task queue); slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, no plan-status job for P2); slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the views); slide 24 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 11 (namespace, task queue, worker versioning as capabilities); slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s). The ownership rulings record job_catalog and interface_config as P2 tables and parameter and reference data as P3, and feature_flag as a platform library object. ADR-023 requires observability per service and gives no threshold. RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG section 12.5 lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration, which the job map and RWB-P3-E2002-APP contradict.
proposed: Approve the three assumptions of RWB-P2-E2002-OPS in the release readiness review: the identity and environment values with no Schedule and no migration, the trigger wiring with the ACE-or-stub record and the corrected harness row, and the five series, four alerts, the named no-package row and the four runbook entries. (11) Switch: feature flags belong to the platform library by the R-PREC default ruling, while the legacy story reads the flag rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing from the case module's own configuration. (12) Storage: DP-15 is in the pattern list of the legacy key while the read copies nothing, so the per-service Flyway sequence is a build dependency for its conventions only.
